subtopic: Parents pressure on career or marriage
passage:
You asked how Gautam and I got married. I'm Jaya, and at twenty-two I came home and told my parents about him. His family belonged to a different community, and my father's face closed like a door. "What will people say? How will they treat you?"

I was furious and nearly packed a bag to say "him or you". My mother stopped me: "First listen to what your father is afraid of." It was fear for me, not hatred of Gautam.

So I gave no ultimatum. For two years Gautam came for Sunday lunch, helped my father mend his radio and never argued. I told them plainly that I would marry him, and that I would never stop visiting them.

At the wedding my father sat stiff at the back. He never said sorry. But he did, once, pass Gautam the last jalebi.

qa.q: What did Gautam help Jaya's father mend?
What was Jaya's father really afraid of?
qa.a: What people would say and how they would treat Jaya. It was fear for Jaya, not hatred of Gautam.

qa.q: What did Jaya do instead of giving an ultimatum?
qa.a: Jaya kept visiting, let Gautam show respect over two years, and said plainly that the marriage would happen while promising never to stop visiting the parents.

qa.q: How might Jaya's father have seen those two years?
qa.a: Probably as slowly showing him that Gautam was steady and kind. Passing him the last jalebi hints at acceptance even without an apology.

grounding: Parents object to Jaya's partner over community; Jaya understands their fear, shows consistency and respect over time, and states what Jaya will not give up.
